relations.subject: J. C. Sutherland
relations.evidence: Colebrooke remained close to his nephew J. C. Sutherland, with whom he shared intellectual interests, policy positions and a free trader’s outlook.

relations.subject: J. C. Sutherland
relations.evidence: Sutherland had produced a translation of two treatises on the Hindu law of adoption ‘under the authoritative sanction of Mr. Colebrooke’s advice’

relations.subject: J. C. Sutherland
relations.evidence: He also took on a position as professor of law at Hindu College and was admitted a pleader in the EIC courts

relations.subject: George Peacock
relations.evidence: George went up to Cambridge in October 1828, under the tutorship of the mathematician George Peacock, who knew and appreciated Colebrooke’s work
